pattern_pdr.note: Posterior 10 Hz alpha, maximal O1/O2, waxing and waning, and blocking when the eyes open at 7 s.

pattern_sleep_spindles.note: Sleep spindles: 13 Hz waxing-waning bursts about 1 s long, maximal centrally (C3/Cz/C4), in N2 sleep.

pattern_k_complex.note: K-complexes: a negative sharp wave followed by a slower positive wave, over 0.5 s in total, maximal frontocentrally; the second is followed by a spindle.

pattern_mu_rhythm.note: Mu rhythm: arciform 9-10 Hz activity over C3 and C4 with the eyes open (posterior alpha is blocked), sharp negative peaks and rounded positive phases.

pattern_wicket_spikes.note: Wicket spikes: trains of 7-8 Hz arciform waves over the left temporal chain in drowsiness, with no after-going slow wave and no disturbance of the background.

pattern_lambda_waves.note: Lambda waves: surface-positive triangular sharp transients at O1/O2 while the eyes are open and scanning; they disappear if the patient looks at a blank surface.

pattern_posts.note: POSTS: runs of surface-positive, sharply contoured occipital transients at about 4 Hz in N2 sleep; spindles mark the sleep stage.

pattern_rmtd.note: RMTD: a run of notched 6 Hz theta over the left mid-temporal region in drowsiness, monomorphic, without evolution in frequency or field.

pattern_bets.note: BETS/BSSS: very small (under 50 uV), very brief spikes with a wide field in N2 sleep, one on each side; no slow wave and no effect on the background.

pattern_vertex_sharp_waves.note: Vertex sharp waves: high-amplitude negative sharp transients maximal at Cz, phase reversing at Cz in the midline chain, in drowsiness.

pattern_fast_alpha_variant.note: Fast alpha variant: posterior rhythm at about twice the alpha frequency (18 Hz) with the same distribution and reactivity, blocking with eye opening at 7.5 s.

pattern_slow_alpha_variant.note: Slow alpha variant: notched 5 Hz posterior waves (a subharmonic of alpha) mixed with alpha, with the same distribution and blocking on eye opening at 7.5 s.

pattern_alpha_squeak.note: Alpha squeak: for a fraction of a second after the eyes close (2 s), posterior alpha is faster (about 12-13 Hz) before settling to its usual frequency.

pattern_midline_theta.note: Midline theta (Ciganek): rhythmic 6 Hz theta confined to Fz-Cz in the waking state, seen in the midline chain only.

pattern_sreda.note: SREDA: a bilateral, parietal-maximal rhythmic discharge in an older adult that begins as slower waves and becomes a sharply contoured 5-6 Hz rhythm, without clinical change or post-ictal slowing.

pattern_14_6_hz_positive_bursts.note: 14- and 6-Hz positive bursts: comb-like positive spikes over the right posterior temporal region at 14 Hz (2 s) and 6 Hz (6 s), clearest referred to the contralateral ear.

pattern_6_hz_spike_wave.note: 6 Hz (phantom) spike-and-wave: a 1-s burst of tiny spikes with 6 Hz waves, low amplitude and posterior (occipital) in a drowsy adult (the FOLD form).

pattern_hypnagogic_hypersynchrony.note: Hypnagogic hypersynchrony: a burst of high-amplitude, diffuse 4 Hz rhythmic waves in a drowsy young child.

pattern_posterior_slow_waves_youth.note: Posterior slow waves of youth: single delta waves fused with the posterior alpha (alpha riding on them), blocking with eye opening at 8.5 s.

pattern_breach_rhythm.note: Breach rhythm: higher-amplitude, sharper arciform 9 Hz activity with extra beta over C4 (a skull defect), without the evolution or after-going slow waves of epileptiform activity.

pattern_photic_driving.note: Photic driving: a posterior response time-locked to each 8 Hz flash, present only during stimulation (between the markers).

pattern_hv_buildup.note: Hyperventilation buildup: diffuse, frontally predominant high-amplitude rhythmic delta in a child during hyperventilation; it should resolve within about a minute after HV ends.

pattern_three_hz_gsw.note: 3 Hz generalized spike-and-wave: a sudden, frontally maximal, regular 3-3.5 Hz spike-and-wave burst on a normal background (typical absence).

pattern_hypsarrhythmia.note: Hypsarrhythmia: very high amplitude, chaotic asynchronous slow waves with multifocal spikes and no organized background, in an infant.

pattern_focal_spikes_temporal.note: Left anterior temporal spikes: phase reversal across F7-T3 (F7 and T3 equally involved, so F7-T3 is nearly flat) with after-going slow waves and a field limited to the left temporal chain.

pattern_focal_spikes_frontal.note: Right frontal spikes: phase reversal at F4 with after-going slow waves, maximal over the right frontal region.

pattern_centrotemporal_spikes.note: Centrotemporal spikes: frequent high-amplitude diphasic spikes maximal at C3/T3 with frontal positivity (a horizontal dipole), activated by sleep, in a school-age child.

pattern_slow_spike_wave.note: Slow spike-and-wave: generalized sharp-and-slow complexes at about 2-2.5 Hz on a slow background (Lennox-Gastaut).

pattern_polyspike_wave.note: Generalized polyspike-and-wave: bursts of several spikes followed by a slow wave, frontally predominant, on a normal background (juvenile myoclonic epilepsy).

pattern_gpfa.note: Generalized paroxysmal fast activity: bursts of 18 Hz fast rhythmic activity (range 10-25 Hz), frontally predominant, in sleep (Lennox-Gastaut tonic seizures).

pattern_pswcs.note: Periodic sharp wave complexes: generalized sharp complexes repeating about once per second on a slow, low background (Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease).

pattern_pleds.note: LPDs (lateralized periodic discharges, formerly PLEDs): sharp-and-slow complexes repeating about every 1.2 s over the left hemisphere, maximal at T3, with a suppressed slow left background.

pattern_sturge_weber.note: Sturge-Weber pattern: attenuated background and polymorphic delta over the affected (right) hemisphere, with normal activity on the left.

pattern_photoparoxysmal.note: Photoparoxysmal response: generalized spike-and-wave triggered by 16 Hz photic stimulation, starting during stimulation and outlasting it by about 1 s.

pattern_tirda.note: TIRDA: runs of rhythmic 2 Hz delta confined to the left anterior temporal region (F7/T3) on a normal background, a marker of temporal lobe epilepsy.

pattern_focal_seizure_temporal.note: Left temporal seizure: rhythmic 7 Hz theta at T3 that slows and grows to high-amplitude 4-5 Hz activity over seconds (evolution in frequency, amplitude and field).

pattern_diffuse_slowing.note: Diffuse slowing: the posterior rhythm is slowed to about 6.5 Hz with abundant diffuse theta and delta over both hemispheres.

pattern_focal_slowing.note: Focal slowing: continuous irregular (polymorphic) delta confined to the left temporal region, with a normal right hemisphere.

pattern_firda.note: FIRDA: runs of rhythmic 2 Hz delta, bifrontally maximal, on a mildly slow background in an encephalopathic adult. In ACNS 2021 terms: frontally predominant GRDA.

pattern_oirda.note: OIRDA: runs of rhythmic 3 Hz delta maximal over the occipital regions in a child (often seen with absence epilepsy).

pattern_triphasic_waves.note: Triphasic waves: blunt complexes with a dominant positive middle phase, frontally maximal with a fronto-occipital lag, on a slow background (metabolic encephalopathy). In ACNS 2021 terms: GPDs with triphasic morphology.

pattern_burst_suppression.note: Burst suppression: bursts of mixed high-amplitude activity with sharp transients alternating with a suppressed (near-flat) background.

pattern_alpha_coma.note: Alpha coma: diffuse, frontally predominant, monotonous 10 Hz alpha in a comatose patient, not reactive to stimulation.

pattern_extreme_delta_brush.note: Extreme delta brush: continuous rhythmic delta with a burst of beta riding on each delta wave, in an adult with anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis.

pattern_eci.note: Electrocerebral inactivity: no cerebral activity over 2 uV at 2 uV/mm; only EKG artifact and instrument noise remain. ECI recordings use double-distance (at least 10 cm) electrode spacing.

pattern_eye_blink.note: Eye blinks: large positive (downward in the Fp1-F7 and Fp2-F8 chains) slow deflections at Fp1/Fp2, symmetric, with no field beyond the frontal poles.

pattern_lateral_eye.note: Lateral eye movements: opposite-polarity deflections at F7 and F8 (looking left at 2 s, right at 6 s), the cornea making the near side positive.

pattern_muscle_artifact.note: Muscle (EMG) artifact: very fast, spiky, high-frequency activity over the temporal regions during jaw clenching, obscuring the background.

pattern_electrode_pop.note: Electrode pop: abrupt, steep deflections with an exponential decay confined to one electrode (T4), with no field and no physiological shape.

pattern_60hz.note: 60 Hz interference: a thick, monotonous band of 60 Hz activity in the channels containing one high-impedance electrode (T4).

pattern_ekg_artifact.note: EKG artifact: small sharp transients time-locked to the QRS in the EKG channel, best seen in ear-referenced and temporal channels.

pattern_glossokinetic.note: Glossokinetic artifact: broad, synchronous delta-like waves largest at the infraorbital leads (IO1/IO2), smaller at Fp1/Fp2, with tongue movement during speech.

pattern_sweat_artifact.note: Sweat artifact: very slow (under 0.5 Hz) high-amplitude sways at a few left frontotemporal electrodes, visible with a low LFF setting.

pattern_photomyogenic.note: Photomyogenic response: frontal muscle spikes time-locked to each 12 Hz flash, confined to Fp/F electrodes and stopping the moment stimulation stops (no cerebral spike-and-wave).

pattern_electrodecrement.note: Infantile spasm (electrodecremental event): a generalized high-amplitude slow wave followed by abrupt attenuation of the hypsarrhythmic background for about 2 s.

pattern_sspe.note: SSPE periodic complexes: stereotyped high-amplitude, generalized slow complexes repeating at long intervals (here about 4.5 s) on a slow background.

pattern_rem_sawtooth.note: REM sleep: a low-voltage mixed-frequency background with rapid conjugate eye movements (opposite deflections at F7 and F8) and a run of notched 3 Hz sawtooth waves over the vertex.

pattern_excess_beta.note: Excess beta (medication effect): abundant 18-25 Hz beta, anterior predominant, over a normal posterior alpha in a patient taking a benzodiazepine.

pattern_pulse_artifact.note: Pulse artifact: a smooth slow wave at one electrode (T4), recurring about 250 ms after every QRS in the EKG channel; moving the electrode off the artery removes it.

pattern_salt_bridge.note: Salt bridge: the F3-C3 channel is nearly flat because sweat or gel connects F3 and C3, so both record the same potential, while the neighbouring channels are normal.

pattern_chewing_artifact.note: Chewing artifact: rhythmic bursts of muscle (EMG) over both temporal regions, one burst with each chew (about 1 per second), with clean background between bursts.

pattern_trace_discontinu.note: Tracé discontinu (prematurity, about 28 weeks PMA): bursts of mixed activity with delta brushes and temporal theta, separated by very low-voltage interburst intervals that at this age often last 10 s or more.

pattern_trace_alternant.note: Tracé alternant (term quiet sleep): high-voltage bursts alternating with lower-voltage (but not flat) interburst activity every few seconds, with frontal sharp transients.

pattern_delta_brushes.note: Delta brushes of prematurity: 0.5-1.5 Hz delta waves with 8-20 Hz fast activity riding on them, central and occipital, abundant around 32-34 weeks PMA.

pattern_temporal_theta_prematurity.note: Temporal theta of prematurity (temporal sawtooth): brief, sharply contoured 4-6 Hz runs over both temporal regions, most prominent at about 26-30 weeks PMA.

pattern_encoches_frontales.note: Encoches frontales: bilateral, synchronous, broad diphasic frontal sharp transients (Fp1/Fp2) in a term newborn, normal around 35-44 weeks PMA, often with anterior slow dysrhythmia.

pattern_neonatal_seizure.note: Neonatal seizure: a focal rhythmic discharge at C3 that slows and grows over seconds (evolution), at least 10 s long in a full recording; neonatal seizures are usually focal and often have no visible clinical sign.

pattern_gpds.note: GPDs (generalized periodic discharges): sharp discharges in both hemispheres at the same moment and similar size, about once per second, each separated by background, in a stuporous patient with renal failure.

pattern_lrda.note: LRDA (lateralized rhythmic delta activity): rhythmic 1.5 Hz delta with no gap between waves over the left temporal region, a 6-s (very brief) run; LRDA is closely linked to seizures.

pattern_bipds.note: BIPDs (bilateral independent periodic discharges): periodic discharges over each hemisphere at the same time but independently, with different rates (about 0.8 Hz on the left, 1.2 Hz on the right) and no fixed time relation.

pattern_birds.note: BIRDs (brief potentially ictal rhythmic discharges): a 1.6-s run of 5.5 Hz rhythmic activity over the left temporal region (over 4 Hz, 0.5 s to under 10 s) matching the patient's seizure onset.

pattern_sirpids.note: SIRPIDs (stimulus-induced): generalized periodic discharges appear right after an alerting stimulus (sternal rub at 3 s) in a comatose patient and were reproducible with repeated stimulation; coded SI-GPDs.

pattern_iic_lpds.note: Ictal-interictal continuum: left LPDs at about 2 Hz (more than 1 and up to 2.5 Hz averaged over 10 s), which meets IIC criterion A without reaching the 2.5 Hz seizure threshold.

pattern_secondary_bilateral_synchrony.note: Secondary bilateral synchrony: each burst starts with a sharp wave at F3 about a tenth of a second before bilateral spike-and-wave that stays left-predominant, so a focal (left frontal) source generalizes rapidly.
